content.value_statement: Database code can become inconsistent across models, sessions, migrations, and queries. This skill supplies reusable SQLModel and SQLAlchemy patterns for reliable async database applications.
actual_capabilities: Sets up asynchronous SQLAlchemy engines, sessions, and connection cleanup.
Provides SQLModel base models with timestamps, validation, and soft-delete fields.
Demonstrates repository CRUD operations with pagination and model attribute checks.
Builds composable filters, joins, grouping, and ordering for application queries.
Shows Alembic migration structures for users, tasks, tags, indexes, and relationships.
Includes local SQLite test-session and production configuration examples.
limitations: Examples require adaptation for your framework, dependency versions, and schema.
The skill does not run migrations, inspect a live database, or manage credentials.
Performance settings are illustrative and require measurement for each deployment.
Some examples target PostgreSQL features and need changes for other database engines.

use_cases.title: Create an async service database layer
use_cases.description: Use the session and repository patterns to add reliable CRUD operations to a Python API.

use_cases.title: Plan a safe schema migration
use_cases.description: Use the migration example to draft tables, constraints, indexes, and rollback steps.

use_cases.title: Improve query performance
use_cases.description: Review query construction, pagination, indexes, and slow-query monitoring patterns.

prompt_templates.title: Start an async database setup
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an async SQLAlchemy database manager for a Python service using DATABASE_URL. Include safe session cleanup and explain the required packages.

prompt_templates.title: Design a SQLModel entity
prompt_templates.prompt: Design SQLModel models for users and tasks. Include timestamps, unique email validation, ownership, soft deletion, and useful indexes.

prompt_templates.title: Add repository queries
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a typed repository for Task with pagination, owner-scoped filtering, status filtering, and safe sort options. State any validation assumptions.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a migration review
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this planned schema change for migration safety. Identify indexes, constraints, rollback steps, locking concerns, and deployment checks: [describe change].

output_examples.input: Create an async database manager for PostgreSQL.
output: Session lifecycle with commit, rollback, and close handling.
A concise list of required environment variables and packages.

output_examples.input: Add an owner-scoped task search with pagination.
output: A query plan that restricts results to the owner.
Recommended indexes for owner, status, and creation time.

output_examples.input: Plan a migration for tags on tasks.
output: A migration outline for tags and the task-tag relation.
Upgrade, rollback, and deployment validation steps.

best_practices: Keep database URLs in environment variables and use separate credentials for each environment.
Use transactions, rollback handling, and bounded pagination for every write or list operation.
Test migrations and representative queries against a staging database before production deployment.
anti_patterns: Do not concatenate user input into raw SQL statements.
Do not expose database credentials in source files, logs, or error responses.
Do not apply destructive migrations without a tested rollback and backup plan.

faq.question: Which databases does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers patterns for PostgreSQL, MySQL, and SQLite through SQLModel and SQLAlchemy examples.

faq.question: Does this skill connect to my database?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and example code only.

faq.question: Can I use it with asynchronous Python services?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill includes async engine and session management patterns.

faq.question: Does it generate Alembic migrations?
faq.answer: It provides migration structures and guidance. Review generated migrations before applying them.

faq.question: Are the performance settings production defaults?
faq.answer: No. Measure workload and database limits before selecting pool sizes, indexes, and timeouts.

faq.question: How should I handle database credentials?
faq.answer: Use environment variables or an approved secret manager. Never place credentials in application source code.
